name: CP2102
description: Highly integrated USB 2.0 full-speed to UART bridge that needs essentially no external components: it includes the USB transceiver, an internal clock/oscillator, an on-chip voltage regulator, and a programmable ROM for the USB VID/PID and serial/description strings. It implements a full UART with all RS-232 modem-control signals and supports 300 bps to 1 Mbps. Silicon Labs provides royalty-free Virtual COM Port drivers. Only offered in a 28-pin QFN (5x5 mm) - no through-hole option. (CP2102N is the recommended pin-compatible successor.)

extra.Vcc: self-powered 3.0-3.6 V (VDD); USB bus-powered 4.0-5.25 V (into REGIN)
extra.exposed_pad: center GND pad must be grounded

typical_application: USB-bus-powered USB-to-UART/RS-232 adapter: VBUS to REGIN through the on-chip 3.3 V regulator feeding VDD, with TXD/RXD/modem lines to the target or an RS-232 transceiver.
gotchas: QFN-28 only (5x5 mm) - there is no DIP/through-hole version, so it needs a breakout board or reflow for hand use
the center exposed pad is GND and must be soldered to the ground plane
bus-powered designs feed 5 V into REGIN and take 3.3 V from VDD; self-powered designs feed 3.0-3.6 V directly into VDD - wire the regulator correctly for your power scheme
pin 18 is NC on the CP2102 but VPP on the CP2109 (EPROM) variant - do not repurpose it if you want cross-compatibility
for Arduino-style auto-reset, DTR is wired through a capacitor to the target reset line (modem signals here are active-low though not named with the # suffix of the FT232R)
the original CP2102 is increasingly hard to source; the pin-compatible CP2102N is the recommended replacement for new designs
